title: Chapter 14: Sabbat
content: Chapter 14: Sabbat

The interrogation room was sterile and impersonal. A sturdy-looking desk was set up, but the chairs were simple folding ones. Perhaps because the room was underground, there were no windows. A one-way mirror was installed on one wall, allowing observation from an adjacent room, though there was no way to confirm if anyone was actually watching.

This time, I was the victim. The heavy-handed treatment seemed excessive for questioning a victim, but considering I was a man who had come to the academy—an outsider—they were understandably cautious.

The ones who detained me on the battlefield were, according to Lieutenant Hayase, members of Sabbat, an internal organization within the academy. My impression of them was that they were a security force specializing in maintaining order within the academy. In fact, I wasn’t far off. The fact they had interrogation rooms was proof enough.

On the battlefield, the Sabbat operatives wore black Battle Dresses, but now they were dressed in black uniforms. Their intimidating uniforms differed in design from those worn by the academy’s female students. They adopted a style reminiscent of police officers, clearly to distinguish themselves from the students.
Most of the operatives appeared to be in their early twenties, and the two members present in the interrogation room looked about my age.

At a small table against the wall, a long-haired woman with narrow eyes was calmly recording my testimony on a laptop. The conversation was being summarized via audio, but she occasionally typed in missing details or points of interest.

The woman directly interrogating me was a short-haired black-haired operative. She gave off a stiff military vibe but seemed to harbor some dissatisfaction toward me, deliberately sitting on the edge of the table. She avoided looking me directly in the face, instead staring down at a binder filled with documents.
“You seemed quite close with Louise. Since you joined Class 5, she’s been taking care of you. It must have been painful to be betrayed, right?”
Her words sounded almost sympathetic, but her gaze was sharp.

“She’s a cruel girl who toyed with your feelings. She got close to you to mislead you, then betrayed you once you hit the battlefield. Well, I suppose it’s foolish to expect anything else. Did you really think a former infantryman could be a match for a rookie Valkyrie?”
She seemed to have some misconceptions, so I spoke up to correct her.
“Being betrayed by a friend was certainly painful. But before even considering whether we were a match, she and I were both students of Class 5. I never thought about matching or not.”

“Are you playing dumb? Or are you too embarrassed to admit it? You must have hoped your relationship with Louise would develop into something more, which is why you were taken advantage of and deceived, right?”

The narrow-eyed woman recording the session chuckled quietly. The woman sitting on the table looked down on me with blatant disdain. They seemed to harbor disgust not just because I was a man, but because I had limbs enhanced with Gijuu cells.
“No, that’s not true. It’s a fact I was deceived, but my relationship with Louise was that of friends. …In front of me, she was pretending to be a friend up until that time.”
I stated the facts without changing my expression, and the woman on the table snorted.

“Stubborn one, aren’t you? Well, fine. Starting tomorrow, we’ll also question the students of Class 5. We’ll see what kind of relationship you and Louise really had. I hope your statements turn out to be true.”
“Yes.”
I replied, and the woman sitting on the table grimaced. She glanced at the narrow-eyed woman.
“There are other things we want to ask, but it’s about time for a break. We have to treat heroes returning from the battlefield with care, even if they are an outsider like you.”

Apparently, it was a rule or an unspoken code among them to treat comrades returning from the battlefield with respect. Their tone suggested they didn’t want to include me in that category, but several hours had already passed since I was brought here. We hadn’t had dinner yet, so perhaps they welcomed the excuse for a break.
The narrow-eyed woman stood up and pulled a smartphone from her pocket, turning it toward me.

“Since this is a special occasion, shall we confirm your order? Is there anything you’d like to eat? How about katsudon? In old detective dramas, it was a classic scene where the culprit eats katsudon and confesses, so it suits you.”
It seemed they wanted to treat me like a criminal.

The short-haired woman put down her binder once, then rested her left hand on the table before picking it up again—a cumbersome motion that caught my attention. She seemed to be protecting her right arm.
“I’m going out first. Once you’ve given your order, you can take a break too.”
“R- Roger.”
The narrow-eyed woman gave a drawn-out reply and a sloppy salute. Once her superior left, she turned her face toward me.
“Come on, hurry up and order. We’re busy here too.”
“I’m at a loss since there’s no menu.”
I was genuinely unsure if ordering katsudon was appropriate. The narrow-eyed woman clicked her tongue.
“At this hour, you can get Japanese, Western, or Chinese food. Oh, would you like to use the vending machines in our building? They even have those awful portable nutrition packs.”
That was probably a joke to her, but I couldn’t ignore the comment.
“Do you have chocolate flavor?”
“Huh? I think so…”

The portable nutrition packs I relied on during my infantry days were block-type foods. They contained a large amount of nutrients necessary for soldiers and were handy when you wanted to finish a meal quickly.

The problem was the taste. Multiple flavors were prepared to avoid monotony, but as infantry, I never had the right to choose. They were randomly included in the consumables handed out before deployment, so I couldn’t pick my preferred flavor.
My favorite was chocolate. It was rated as the most “edible” flavor and was highly valuable in nutrition pack trades.
Personally, I thought it tasted good, but these packs prioritized nutrition over flavor. Most infantry ate them because they had no choice.
Still, there was a problem. Someone seemed to have taken the chocolate flavor before distribution, so it was rarely available. When I was lucky enough to get some, I savored it carefully.
Looking back now, I guess I was just greedy.
“R- Really, is this okay? There are plenty of other options besides katsudon, you know?”

The narrow-eyed woman held out a chocolate-flavored nutrition pack in front of me. It was wrapped in silver foil with a simple sticker showing a chocolate illustration. The packaging was familiar from the surface world.
I took it with both hands, carefully tearing it open from the cut, and pulled out the contents.
The block-shaped food stained chocolate brown stirred a wave of nostalgia and happiness within me. Soldiers often fought over these packs. It was a sinful treat, a rare delicacy for me.
“I’ll eat it.”
After steadying my breath, I bit into the chocolate flavor. As it entered my mouth, a dry, saliva-absorbing texture spread along with a faint chocolate taste.
It was an excellent food that provided plenty of calories along with nutrition, but it was unpopular due to its difficulty to eat and poor taste. The mint flavor was especially awful.
I disliked mint, but even when hungry, I hesitated to eat it because it was so unpleasant.
My attachment to the chocolate flavor and hatred of mint suggested I was quite picky.
As I chewed the chocolate flavor, the narrow-eyed woman looked at me in disbelief.
“Y- You really look like you’re enjoying it…”
She wore an expression of incredulity.
After a while, the break ended, and the short-haired woman returned. She still moved as if protecting her right arm, but the moment she entered the room, her face turned startled.
She immediately confronted the narrow-eyed woman.
“Hey! Even if he’s an enemy, we were ordered by the principal to handle him carefully! What you did is out of line!”
She was pointing at the chocolate flavor I was eating, but the narrow-eyed woman hurriedly shook her head.
“N- No! I checked multiple times, but he insisted this was fine!”
The narrow-eyed woman testified to her innocence. The short-haired woman grimaced and turned back to me.
“Is that true?”
“Yes. When I was fighting on the surface, chocolate flavor was precious, so I ordered it. Did I cause trouble?”
I felt sorry if I had caused any, but the other woman was flustered.
“No, it’s not trouble exactly… Are you sane? What do you usually eat to survive?”
The two women huddled together. They seemed terrified by something they couldn’t understand.
Once again misunderstood, I decided to clarify.
“I eat the meals prepared by the development team. They’re always nutrition-focused, and while they’re blander than what I had on the surface, there’s no problem.”
I told them I was normal, but they refused to accept it. Whispering to each other, the short-haired woman kept glancing at me.
“Could it be a side effect of the experiment affecting your taste?”
“Considering how you’re enjoying such awful nutrition packs, probably.”
The misunderstanding wasn’t cleared up. It seemed I lacked social skills. If only I could imitate the MC, the hair stylist, or the loser’s casual banter, maybe I could get through this.
The short-haired woman sent the narrow-eyed woman away, leaving just the two of us. Instead of sitting at the desk, she took the folding chair placed in front of me.
“Well then, let’s continue the interrogation.”
“You seem to have injured your right arm. Are you okay?”
She frowned and glared at me, as if she hadn’t noticed my concern. Had I hurt her pride by worrying about her? Just as I thought I’d failed again, her expression turned more serious.
“…It was a training accident. Want to hear about my blunders?”
“That’s not what I meant.”
“Don’t interrupt me. Let’s get this over with. I don’t intend to spend forever with you.”
She went from showing raw emotion to simply doing her job. It seemed I was thoroughly disliked.
